entries.rationale: the caller (lowerSubqueryOverAggregate) pre-filters to the supported aggregation op set before consulting this builder

entries.head: promql
entries.message: promql: subquery over %T is unsupported
entries.rationale: SubqueryExpr.Expr must type-check as an instant vector, and every instant-vector AST shape is dispatched (selector, call, paren, aggregate, binary, unary, plus the parser-impossible nested SubqueryExpr handled defensively); scalar- and string-typed inners are parse-time type errors.

entries.head: promql
entries.message: promql: subquery over aggregation of %T is unsupported
entries.rationale: An aggregation's argument must type-check as an instant vector, and every instant-vector AST shape is dispatched (paren, call, selector, binary, unary, nested aggregate); scalar- and string-typed inners are parse-time type errors.

entries.head: promql
entries.message: promql: subquery over absent() requires query eval-time context (use LowerAt)
entries.rationale: The HTTP handlers always thread eval times via LowerAt / LowerAtRange; only the raw Lower() entrypoint (tests / tooling) can present a zero eval anchor to this guard.

entries.head: promql
entries.message: promql: subquery over %s aggregation is not supported
entries.rationale: every parser aggregation op is dispatched by the switch above this default arm (the eight per-bucket reducers plus quantile, topk/bottomk/limitk, limit_ratio and count_values), so no parseable query reaches it

entries.head: promql
entries.message: promql: subquery inner %s expects exactly %d argument(s), got %d
entries.rationale: parser-enforced arity: every function in the subquery-inner shape table is pinned at its argument count in parser.Functions, so the lowering never observes a different one

entries.message: promql: subquery `@ start()` modifier requires query range context (use LowerAt)
entries.rationale: the query endpoints always lower via LowerAtRange with the request window, so range context is always present
